title: The Lesson I Learned From the Donkey That Saw the Angel First
paragraphs:
The Lesson I Learned From the Donkey That Saw the Angel First
(Numbers 22:23)
He looked foolish.
Until he was the only one seeing clearly.
Numbers 22:23 says, “When the donkey saw the angel of the Lord standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand, she turned off the road into a field…”
Let that sink in.

The prophet was blind.
The donkey was not.
That broke me.

Because sometimes the loudest person in the room is the last one to notice God is trying to stop them. Sometimes we are so locked into our ambition, our plans, our “I know what I’m doing” energy, that we call resistance a problem—when it is actually mercy.

Balaam kept pushing.
The donkey kept resisting.
And the donkey was right.
Here’s the lesson: not every delay is the devil. Not every closed door is an attack. Sometimes God lets the donkey stop because the angel ahead has a sword, not applause.
And that’s where grace walks in.

God did not block Balaam to destroy him.
God blocked Balaam to warn him.

Some of us are frustrated because life is not moving.
But what if Heaven is protecting you from a road your flesh is eager to take?
What if the thing you’re mad at is the very thing God is using to save you?

The donkey saw the danger first.
Balaam saw it later.
And pride always hates being corrected by unexpected messengers.
But the wise learn.

God can use a sermon.
God can use a child.
God can use a failure.
God can even use a donkey.

So before you force the door, pray.
Before you curse the interruption, listen.
Before you assume you see clearly, kneel.
Because Jesus is not only the Savior who forgives our wrong turns—He is also the Shepherd who blocks deadly paths we cannot yet see.

That is mercy.
That is love.
That is grace.

If God is slowing you down right now, do not despise the pause.
It may be the holiest protection in your life.
